questions.stem:

questions.stem:

FLOCK : SHEEP :: SCHOOL : ___
questions.explanation: A flock is a group of sheep; a school is a group of fish.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: An archipelago is a group of islands; a constellation is a group of stars.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: An illiterate person cannot read; a mute person cannot speak.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
PREFACE : BOOK :: OVERTURE : ___
questions.explanation: A preface opens a book; an overture opens an opera.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
SECOND : MINUTE :: MINUTE : ___

WATER : THIRST

questions.stem:
Choose the pair whose relationship is most similar to that of the capitalized pair.
BRAVE : COWARDLY
questions.explanation: Brave and cowardly are opposites, like generous and stingy. The other pairs are synonyms.

EVAPORATE : VAPOR :: FREEZE : ___

questions.stem:

WORD : SENTENCE :: SENTENCE : ___

questions.stem:

NOVICE : EXPERT :: APPRENTICE : ___

MAYOR : CITY

PUPPY : DOG :: KITTEN : ___
questions.explanation: A puppy is a young dog; a kitten is a young cat.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.

questions.stem:
Complete the analogy.
PAGE : BOOK :: BRICK : ___

questions.stem:

questions.stem:

AUTHOR : NOVEL :: COMPOSER : ___

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "The city will hire more traffic enforcers to ease congestion during the holidays."
choices: Additional traffic enforcers can help reduce congestion.
All drivers in the city violate traffic rules.
Traffic enforcers are paid more than other employees.
There will be no traffic after the holidays.
questions.explanation: Hiring enforcers "to ease congestion" only makes sense if more enforcers can actually help reduce it.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "Please bring two valid IDs when you claim your package."
choices: Packages can also be claimed online.
Packages are often claimed by the wrong person.
The office needs to confirm who is claiming the package.
Most claimants forget to bring their IDs.
questions.explanation: Asking for IDs assumes the office needs to confirm the identity of the person claiming.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "Apply early to avoid the long lines on the last day of filing."
choices: Many applicants file on the last day.
The filing deadline will be extended.
Lines are short on the last day.
questions.explanation: The advice assumes lines are long on the last day, which happens when many people file then.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "The school will offer free tutoring sessions to improve students' reading scores."
choices: Tutoring can help improve students' reading.
Teachers do not know how to teach reading.
All students are currently failing reading.
questions.explanation: Offering tutoring "to improve" scores assumes tutoring can help. Nothing suggests that all students are failing.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "Our water filter removes 99% of bacteria. Buy one to keep your family safe."
choices: The water a family uses may contain harmful bacteria.
Bacteria can be seen with the naked eye.
Boiling water does not kill bacteria.
Most families already own a water filter.
questions.explanation: Removing bacteria keeps a family "safe" only if the water they use may contain harmful bacteria. The ad does not depend on any claim about boiling or on how many families own filters.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "The library extended its hours until 9 p.m. to serve working students."
choices: Some working students can visit only in the evening.
The library is busiest in the morning.
Most library users are working students.
Working students prefer e-books to printed books.
questions.explanation: Extending evening hours for working students assumes that some of them can come only after work or class.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "Employees are reminded to turn off the lights and air conditioners before leaving, to reduce electricity costs."
choices: Leaving appliances on adds to electricity costs.
Employees never go home on time.
The office has no air conditioners.
questions.explanation: The reminder assumes that appliances left on use electricity that adds to the bill.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "To reduce the spread of dengue, residents are urged to remove stagnant water around their homes."
choices: Most residents keep their surroundings clean.
Dengue cases rise mainly during the dry season.
Mosquitoes that spread dengue can breed in stagnant water.
Dengue spreads mainly through contaminated food.
questions.explanation: Removing stagnant water reduces dengue only if mosquitoes that spread it breed in such water.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "The company will post its job openings on social media to reach more applicants."
choices: The company has never hired anyone before.
Many potential applicants use social media.
Social media posts never contain errors.
questions.explanation: Posting on social media "to reach more applicants" assumes many potential applicants are there.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "Read the instructions carefully before answering the test."
choices: Most test takers usually skip the instructions.
Test takers who read slowly will not finish the test.
Reading the instructions can help test takers answer correctly.
The test has more questions than usual this year.
questions.explanation: The advice assumes the instructions contain information that affects how to answer.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "Bring an umbrella; the forecast says it will rain this afternoon."
choices: The weather forecast is reasonably reliable.
questions.explanation: The advice relies on the forecast, so it assumes the forecast can be trusted.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "The agency replaced its paper forms with online forms to speed up processing."
choices: Online forms can be processed faster than paper forms.
All of the paper forms were lost.
Online forms are longer than paper forms.
Clients prefer to visit the office in person.
questions.explanation: Switching "to speed up processing" assumes online forms are faster to process.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "Wear a helmet; it could save your life in an accident."
choices: Riders without helmets are more likely to have accidents.
Helmets can reduce the risk of serious head injury.
Helmets are required by law for all riders.
questions.explanation: The claim that a helmet "could save your life" assumes it protects the head in an accident. It does not assume helmets prevent accidents or that a law requires them.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "The new evacuation center will be built on higher ground."
choices: The mayor lives on higher ground.
The old center was too large.
Higher ground is less likely to be flooded.
questions.explanation: Choosing higher ground for an evacuation center assumes it is safer from floods.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an assumption implicit in the statement?
Statement: "Students who want to join the debate team must first pass an audition."
choices: Most students who audition are good speakers.
Students who pass the audition will win debates.
The debate team has more members than other clubs.
Not every student who wants to join will be accepted.
questions.explanation: Requiring an audition implies screening, which assumes some who want to join may not get in.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
All employees in the records section have completed the data privacy training. Jose works in the records section.
choices: Jose will conduct the next training.
Jose has completed the data privacy training.
Jose is the head of the records section.
Only the records section took the training.
questions.explanation: If all records section employees completed the training and Jose is one of them, he completed it.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
In a survey of 500 commuters, 80% said they would use a bike lane if one were built along the main road.
choices: The city government has approved the bike lane.
Most residents of the city already own a bicycle.
A bike lane will reduce traffic on the main road.
Many of the surveyed commuters are open to biking on the main road.
questions.explanation: The survey only shows what respondents said they would do. Whether a lane would reduce traffic, how many residents own bikes, or whether the lane is approved is not shown.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
Sales of electric fans in the province this April were double those of last April.
choices: More electric fans were sold this April than last April.
This April was the hottest month in history.
Every household in the province bought a new fan.
Air conditioners are no longer sold in the province.
questions.explanation: Doubled sales directly mean more fans were sold. The other choices may or may not be true; the data alone does not show them.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
Since the barangay installed streetlights on Mabini Street, reported thefts there have dropped by half.
choices: The drop in thefts on Mabini Street came after the lights were installed.
Thefts have increased on streets without new lights.
The streetlights caused thefts on Mabini Street to drop.
No thefts have occurred on Mabini Street since then.
questions.explanation: The information shows only that thefts fell by half after the lights went up. That timing alone does not prove the lights caused the drop; other changes could explain it. Thefts did not stop entirely, and nothing is said about other streets.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
Only applicants with at least two years of experience will be interviewed. Maria has one year of experience.
choices: Maria has more experience than the other applicants.
questions.explanation: Maria has less than two years of experience, so she does not qualify for an interview.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
Every committee member voted, and the proposal passed by a majority of the votes.
choices: All members voted in favor of the proposal.
More than half of the votes were in favor of the proposal.
questions.explanation: A majority means more than half. A majority does not require every vote, and every member did vote.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
The bus leaves the terminal every 30 minutes, starting at 6:00 a.m. Ana arrived at the terminal at 7:10 a.m.
choices: Ana arrived just in time for the 7:00 a.m. bus.
The next bus after Ana arrived leaves at 7:15 a.m.
The next bus after Ana arrived leaves at 8:00 a.m.
The next bus after Ana arrived leaves at 7:30 a.m.
questions.explanation: Buses leave at 6:00, 6:30, 7:00, 7:30, and so on. The 7:00 bus had already left when Ana arrived at 7:10, so the next is 7:30.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
Ramon is older than Liza. Liza is older than Carlo.
choices: Carlo is the oldest of the three.
Liza is the youngest of the three.
Ramon and Carlo are the same age.
questions.explanation: Ramon > Liza > Carlo in age, so Ramon is older than Carlo.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
Most of the residents who attended the town hall meeting supported the new market project.
choices: Most residents of the town support the project.
The project had support among the residents who attended.
Residents who did not attend oppose the project.
The project will be approved by the town council.
questions.explanation: "Most" of the attendees supported it. That does not mean every resident or every attendee did.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
Of the 40 employees in the office, 25 take the bus to work and 10 drive. The rest walk.
questions.explanation: 40 − 25 − 10 = 5 employees walk.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
Documents submitted after the deadline will not be processed. Pedro's documents were processed.
choices: Pedro submitted his documents on or before the deadline.
Pedro submitted his documents after the deadline.
Pedro was not required to submit documents.
questions.explanation: Late documents are never processed. Pedro's were processed, so they were not late.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
The price of a sack of rice rose by 10% in January and then fell by 10% in February.
choices: At the end of February, the price was the same as at the start of January.
At the end of February, the price was 20% lower than at the start of January.
At the end of February, the price was slightly lower than at the start of January.
At the end of February, the price was higher than at the start of January.
questions.explanation: A price of 100 becomes 110 after a 10% rise, then 110 × 0.90 = 99 after a 10% fall: slightly lower than the start.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
In a class of 30, every student who scored above 90 received a medal. Twelve students received medals.
choices: At most twelve students scored above 90.
questions.explanation: Everyone above 90 got a medal, so there can be no more than 12 such students. Medals may also have gone to others, so it may be fewer than 12.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
Whenever the river rises above the warning level, classes in the town are suspended. Classes were held today.
choices: The river rose above the warning level today.
The river did not rise above the warning level today.
questions.explanation: If the river had risen above the warning level, classes would have been suspended. They were held, so it did not.

questions.stem:
Which conclusion is best supported by the information given?
Ana finished the report before Ben did. Carlo finished after Ben did.
choices: Ana and Carlo finished at the same time.
questions.explanation: The order is Ana, then Ben, then Carlo, so Ana finished before Carlo.

questions.stem:
Assume both statements are true.
No cyclists are photographers. Some singers are cyclists.
Which conclusion necessarily follows?
questions.explanation: Both statements together force it: there is no way to arrange the groups so that both are true and all singers are photographers. "All photographers are singers." does not follow: both statements can be true while some photographers are not singers. "Some photographers are singers." does not follow: both statements can be true while no photographers are singers. "No singers are photographers." does not follow: both statements can be true while some singers are photographers.

questions.stem:

Which conclusion necessarily follows?
questions.explanation: Both statements together force it: there is no way to arrange the groups so that both are true and no collectors are joggers. "Some collectors are not joggers." does not follow: both statements can be true while all collectors are joggers. "All joggers are collectors." does not follow: both statements can be true while some joggers are not collectors. "No collectors are joggers." does not follow: both statements can be true while some collectors are joggers.
