Although he was the newest member of the team, his suggestions were the most ___ by the director.
questions.explanation: "Although" sets up a contrast with being the newest member, so his suggestions were unexpectedly valued.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The clerk was ___ for misplacing the documents a second time.
questions.explanation: Repeating a mistake earns a scolding: reprimanded.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The two witnesses gave ___ accounts, so the investigator could not tell which one was true.
questions.explanation: The investigator could not tell which was true only if the accounts disagreed: conflicting.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
To ___ traffic during the holidays, the city opened alternate routes.
questions.explanation: Alternate routes are opened to lessen traffic: ease.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The rules apply to all employees, ___ of rank.
questions.explanation: "Regardless of rank" means the rank does not matter, which fits rules that apply to all employees.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
Her ___ manner made her popular with clients; she always greeted them with a smile.
questions.explanation: Greeting clients with a smile describes a warm, friendly manner: cordial.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The project was ___ because the funds ran out halfway through.
questions.explanation: Running out of funds halfway means the project was stopped: abandoned.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The speaker was so ___ that the audience began to fall asleep.
questions.explanation: An audience falls asleep when a speaker is dull and unvaried: monotonous.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The agency aims to ___ the processing time from ten days to three.
questions.explanation: Going from ten days to three is a reduction.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The suspect's alibi was ___ by three witnesses who saw him at the party.
questions.explanation: Witnesses who saw him where he claimed to be support his alibi: they corroborated it.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The supervisor gave ___ instructions, so no one knew exactly what to do.
questions.explanation: If no one knew exactly what to do, the instructions were unclear: vague.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
Not only did the volunteers clean the plaza, ___ they also planted trees.
questions.explanation: The correlative pair is "not only ... but also."

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
She studied hard; ___, she passed the exam on her first try.
questions.explanation: Passing is the result of studying hard, so a cause-and-effect connector fits: consequently.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The road was closed; ___, we had to take a longer route.
questions.explanation: Taking a longer route is the result of the closure: therefore.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The building is old; ___, it is still structurally sound.
questions.explanation: Being sound despite its age is a contrast, so a contrast connector fits: nevertheless.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
Applicants must submit their documents ___ the end of the month.
questions.explanation: "By" marks a deadline: no later than the end of the month.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The committee will ___ the proposal before making a final decision.
questions.explanation: Before deciding, the committee examines the proposal closely: scrutinize. Approving it would already be the decision.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
Water is ___ during the dry season, so residents are asked to conserve it.
questions.explanation: Residents are asked to conserve water because there is little of it: scarce.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The old law has been ___; it no longer has any effect.
questions.explanation: A law that no longer has any effect has been repealed. An amended law still has effect in its changed form.

questions.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
The manager was ___ about the plan at first, but she eventually supported it.
questions.explanation: "But she eventually supported it" signals she doubted it at first: skeptical.

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
[Each of the] clerks [have submitted] their reports [on time].
questions.explanation: The subject is "Each," which is singular, so the verb should be "has submitted."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The committee [has decided] to [postpone] the meeting [until next week].
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: "committee" acting as one body takes the singular "has decided."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
[Neither] the supervisor nor the employees [was] informed [about] the change.
questions.explanation: With "neither ... nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "employees," so it should be "were."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
She [has worked] in the agency [since] five years [now].
questions.explanation: A length of time takes "for": "for five years." "Since" goes with a starting point, such as "since 2020."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The documents [were laid] on the table [by] the secretary [yesterday].
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: "laid" is the right past participle of "lay" (to put something down).

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
If he [would have studied] harder, he [could have passed] [the exam].
questions.explanation: In a past unreal condition, the if-clause uses the past perfect: "If he had studied harder."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The new rules apply to [everyone] [except] [he] and the director.
questions.explanation: "Except" is a preposition, so the pronoun after it must be in object form: "except him."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
Please [submit] the forms [to] the office [at] Monday.
questions.explanation: Days take the preposition "on": "on Monday."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The number of complaints [have increased] [since] the new system [was introduced].
questions.explanation: "The number of" is singular, so the verb should be "has increased."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The applicants [who's] documents are incomplete [will be] notified [by email].
questions.explanation: "Who's" means "who is." The possessive form is "whose documents."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
[Its] important to [keep] copies of all receipts [for] the audit.
questions.explanation: "It is important" contracts to "It's." "Its" is the possessive form.

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The team [is planning] [to visit] the province [next month].
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct.

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
He [don't] know [where] the files [are kept].
questions.explanation: A third-person singular subject takes "doesn't": "He doesn't know."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
Between you and [I], the plan [has] [little chance] of success.
questions.explanation: "Between" is a preposition, so it takes the object pronoun: "between you and me."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The manager asked [whether] the report [had been] [finish].
questions.explanation: After "had been," the verb must be the past participle: "had been finished."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
[Less] people attended the seminar [than] we [had expected].
questions.explanation: "People" can be counted, so it takes "fewer," not "less."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The clerk [lended] me [her] pen [during] the exam.
questions.explanation: The past tense of "lend" is "lent."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The [principal] reason for the delay [was] the [lack] of funds.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: "principal" as an adjective means main or chief.

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The seminar [was attended] by [more then] fifty [participants].
questions.explanation: Comparisons use "than": "more than fifty." "Then" refers to time.

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
He is [more taller] than [his] brother [in every photo].
questions.explanation: "Taller" is already comparative; adding "more" is a double comparative.

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The guard [checked] the IDs [carefully] and [let] us in.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: "let" is both the present and the past tense form.

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The secretary [has went] to the bank [to deposit] the [checks].
questions.explanation: After "has," the verb takes the past participle: "has gone."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The reports [was] [submitted] [late] by the field office.
questions.explanation: The plural subject "reports" takes the plural verb "were."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
The [childrens'] [toys] were donated [to] the day care center.
questions.explanation: "Children" is already plural, so the possessive is "children's."

questions.stem:
Which bracketed part of the sentence contains an error? If there is none, choose "No error."
One of the [proposals] [were] [approved] by the board.
questions.explanation: The subject is "One," which is singular, so the verb should be "was approved." "Of the proposals" does not change the subject.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
MALIGAYA ang mga empleyado nang ianunsiyo ang bagong benepisyo.
questions.explanation: Ang maligaya ay nangangahulugang masaya (happy).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Tinulungan ng pamahalaan ang mga pamilyang MARALITA sa lungsod.
questions.explanation: Ang maralita ay nangangahulugang mahirap o dukha (poor).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Ang kanyang DALISAY na hangarin ay makatulong sa kapwa.
questions.explanation: Ang dalisay ay nangangahulugang wagas o puro (pure, sincere).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Kahit mataas na ang kanyang posisyon, nanatili siyang MAPAGKUMBABA.
questions.explanation: Ang mapagkumbaba ay nangangahulugang mababang-loob (humble), ang kabaligtaran ng mayabang.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Siya ay itinuturing na HUWARANG kawani ng tanggapan.
questions.explanation: Ang huwaran ay nangangahulugang uliran o modelo (exemplary, a model to follow).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Pinag-usapan sa pulong ang mga SULIRANIN ng barangay.
questions.explanation: Ang suliranin ay nangangahulugang problema (problem).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Nagsagawa ng masusing PAGSISIYASAT ang komite sa reklamo.
questions.explanation: Ang pagsisiyasat ay nangangahulugang imbestigasyon o pagsusuri (investigation).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
MASIDHI ang kanyang pagnanais na makapasa sa pagsusulit.
questions.explanation: Ang masidhi ay nangangahulugang matindi o malakas (intense).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Nagbabala ang mga awtoridad tungkol sa PANGANIB na dala ng bagyo.
questions.explanation: Ang panganib ay nangangahulugang peligro (danger).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Lumaki ang mga bata sa KALINGA ng kanilang lola.
questions.explanation: Ang kalinga ay nangangahulugang pag-aaruga o pag-aalaga (care).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Nanatiling MAHINAHON ang kawani kahit galit ang kliyente.
questions.explanation: Ang mahinahon ay nangangahulugang kalmado (calm, composed).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
MATAYOG ang mga pangarap ng batang iskolar.
questions.explanation: Ang matayog ay nangangahulugang mataas (lofty, high).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Unti-unting NAGLALAHO ang mga punong bakawan sa baybayin.
questions.explanation: Ang naglalaho ay nangangahulugang nawawala (disappearing, vanishing).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Ang PAMAHALAAN ay may tungkuling pangalagaan ang kapakanan ng mamamayan.
questions.explanation: Ang pamahalaan ay nangangahulugang gobyerno (government).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Pinarusahan ang TAMPALASANG lalaki na nanakit sa matanda.
questions.explanation: Ang tampalasan ay nangangahulugang walang-galang o mapang-abuso (insolent, abusive).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasalungat ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Ang negosyante ay MAYAMAN.
questions.explanation: Ang kasalungat ng mayaman (rich) ay mahirap (poor). Ang masagana ay kasingkahulugan, hindi kasalungat.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasalungat ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
Ang kawani ay MAGALANG sa lahat ng kliyente.
questions.explanation: Ang kasalungat ng magalang (respectful) ay bastos (rude).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasalungat ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
MATAPANG na hinarap ng bumbero ang apoy.
questions.explanation: Ang kasalungat ng matapang (brave) ay duwag (cowardly).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasalungat ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
MASAGANA ang ani ng mga magsasaka ngayong taon.
questions.explanation: Ang kasalungat ng masagana (abundant) ay salat (lacking, scarce).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang kasalungat ng salitang nakasulat sa malalaking titik.
MAKUPAD kumilos ang bagong empleyado.
questions.explanation: Ang makupad (sluggish, slow) ay kasalungat ng maliksi (quick, nimble). Ang mabagal ay kasingkahulugan.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Tumakbo ___ mabilis ang bata.
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang "nang" bilang pang-abay na naglalarawan kung paano ginawa ang kilos (tumakbo nang mabilis).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Bumili siya ___ bagong sapatos.
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang "ng" bago ang pangngalang tinatanggap ng pandiwa (bumili ng sapatos).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
___ dumating ang direktor, nagsimula na ang pulong.
questions.explanation: Ang "nang" sa simula ng sugnay ay nangangahulugang "noong" o "when": Nang dumating ang direktor.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Nag-aral siya ___ mabuti kaya siya pumasa.
questions.explanation: Pang-abay ang "nang mabuti" dahil inilalarawan nito kung paano siya nag-aral.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Kumain ___ mangga ang bata.
questions.explanation: "Ng" ang ginagamit bago ang pangngalang tinatanggap ng pandiwa (kumain ng mangga).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Kain ___ kain ang bata kaya siya tumaba.
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang "nang" sa pagitan ng inuulit na pandiwa: kain nang kain.

questions.stem: Alin sa mga sumusunod na pangungusap ang wasto?
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang "din" kapag katinig ang huling titik ng sinusundang salita, at "rin" kapag patinig o w/y. Nagtatapos sa g ang "masipag," kaya tama ang "din." Dapat "masaya rin," "malakas din," at "matalino rin."

questions.stem: Alin sa mga sumusunod na pangungusap ang wasto?
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang "raw" pagkatapos ng patinig o w/y, at "daw" pagkatapos ng katinig. Nagtatapos sa i ang "uuwi," kaya tama ang "raw." Dapat "aalis daw," "darating daw," at "tapos daw."

questions.stem: Alin sa mga sumusunod na pangungusap ang wasto?
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang "mayroon" kapag sinusundan ng panghalip (siya), at kinakabitan ito ng pang-angkop: "mayroon siyang." Ginagamit naman ang "may" kapag direktang sinusundan ng pangngalan, pandiwa, o pang-uri.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Ito ang aklat ___ binili kahapon.
questions.explanation: Ang "kong" ay "ko" + pang-angkop na "-ng": aklat kong binili (ang aklat na binili ko).

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Hindi ko alam ___ darating siya.
questions.explanation: Ang "kung" ay pangatnig na nangangahulugang "if" o "whether."

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
___ Ana at Ben ay pupunta sa Maynila.
questions.explanation: "Sina" ang pantukoy para sa dalawa o higit pang pangalan ng tao; "si" ay para sa iisa.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Ibigay mo ang sulat ___ Maria.
questions.explanation: "Kay" ang ginagamit bago ang iisang pangalan ng tao bilang tagatanggap; "kina" ay para sa dalawa o higit pa.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Matibay ang bahay ___ bato.
questions.explanation: Ginagamit ang pang-angkop na "na" kapag nagtatapos sa katinig (maliban sa n) ang salitang inaangkupan: bahay na bato.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Bukas, ___ kami sa probinsya.
questions.explanation: "Bukas" ay tumutukoy sa hinaharap, kaya aspektong kontemplatibo ang kailangan: pupunta.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Kahapon, ___ ang mga empleyado sa seminar.
questions.explanation: "Kahapon" ay tumutukoy sa nakaraan, kaya aspektong perpektibo ang kailangan: dumalo.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Araw-araw ___ si Liza ng ehersisyo.
questions.explanation: "Araw-araw" ay nagpapakita ng kilos na nagaganap nang paulit-ulit, kaya aspektong imperpektibo ang kailangan: gumagawa.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Si Ramon ang ___ sa kanilang magkakapatid.
questions.explanation: Paghahambing sa lahat ng magkakapatid ito, kaya pasukdol ang kailangan: pinakamatangkad.

questions.stem:
Piliin ang angkop na salita upang mabuo ang pangungusap.
Si Ben ay ___ ni Carlo; pareho silang 170 sentimetro.
questions.explanation: Magkapantay ang taas nila, kaya paghahambing na magkatulad ang kailangan: kasintangkad.

questions.stem:
Basahin ang talata at sagutin ang tanong.

Ang wika ay hindi lamang kasangkapan sa pakikipag-usap. Ito rin ay salamin ng kultura at kasaysayan ng isang bayan. Sa mga salitang ginagamit natin, makikita kung paano mag-isip, magpahalaga, at makipag-ugnayan ang ating mga ninuno. Kaya kapag nawala ang isang wika, nawawala rin ang bahagi ng ating pagkakakilanlan.

Ano ang pangunahing ideya ng talata?
choices: Ang wika ay salamin ng kultura at pagkakakilanlan ng isang bayan.
Ang wika ay ginagamit lamang sa pakikipag-usap.
Mahirap pag-aralan ang mga lumang wika.
questions.explanation: Sinasabi ng talata na ang wika ay "salamin ng kultura at kasaysayan" at bahagi ng ating pagkakakilanlan.

questions.stem:

Ayon sa talata, ano ang nangyayari kapag nawala ang isang wika?
choices: Nawawala rin ang bahagi ng ating pagkakakilanlan.
questions.explanation: Sinasabi sa huling pangungusap: "nawawala rin ang bahagi ng ating pagkakakilanlan."

Ang salitang "ninuno" sa talata ay nangangahulugang:
questions.explanation: Ang "ninuno" ay ang mga taong nauna sa atin sa angkan o lahi (ancestors).

Basahin ang talata at sagutin ang tanong.

Tuwing tag-ulan, maraming lugar sa Kamaynilaan ang binabaha. Isa sa mga dahilan nito ang mga baradong kanal na puno ng plastik at iba pang basura. Kung matututo ang bawat pamilya na itapon nang wasto ang kanilang basura, malaki ang mababawas sa pagbaha. Hindi sapat na umasa lamang sa pamahalaan; kailangan ang pakikiisa ng lahat.

Ayon sa talata, ano ang isa sa mga dahilan ng pagbaha?
choices: mga baradong kanal na puno ng basura
ang pagdami ng mga sasakyan sa lansangan
ang kakulangan ng mga pumping station
ang pagputol ng mga puno sa kabundukan
questions.explanation: Sinasabi ng talata na "isa sa mga dahilan nito ang mga baradong kanal na puno ng plastik at iba pang basura."

Ano ang nais iparating ng may-akda?
choices: Pamahalaan lamang ang may pananagutan sa pagbaha.
Kailangan ang pakikiisa ng bawat mamamayan upang mabawasan ang pagbaha.
Hindi na malulutas ang problema sa pagbaha.
Dapat lumipat ng tirahan ang mga taga-Maynila.
questions.explanation: Sinasabi ng huling pangungusap na hindi sapat ang umasa sa pamahalaan; "kailangan ang pakikiisa ng lahat."

Ang salitang "pakikiisa" ay nangangahulugang:
questions.explanation: Ang "pakikiisa" ay ang pakikipagtulungan o pakikibahagi sa isang layunin.

Si Aling Nena ay nagtitinda ng gulay sa palengke sa loob ng tatlumpung taon. Maaga siyang gumigising araw-araw upang makakuha ng sariwang paninda mula sa mga magsasaka. Dahil sa kanyang sipag at katapatan sa timbang, marami siyang suki na hindi na lumilipat sa ibang tindera.

Bakit marami ang suki ni Aling Nena?
choices: Dahil siya lamang ang nagtitinda ng gulay
Dahil malapit ang kanyang puwesto sa sakayan
Dahil sa kanyang sipag at katapatan sa timbang
questions.explanation: Sinasabi ng talata: "Dahil sa kanyang sipag at katapatan sa timbang, marami siyang suki."

Ang salitang "suki" ay tumutukoy sa:
questions.explanation: Ang "suki" ay mamimiling palaging bumibili sa iisang tindera.

Ipinagdiriwang ang Buwan ng Wika tuwing Agosto. Sa buwang ito, nagsasagawa ang mga paaralan ng iba't ibang gawain tulad ng sabayang pagbigkas, balagtasan, at paligsahan sa pagsulat ng sanaysay. Layunin nitong palalimin ang pagmamahal ng mga kabataan sa wikang Filipino at sa iba pang katutubong wika ng bansa.

Kailan ipinagdiriwang ang Buwan ng Wika ayon sa talata?
questions.explanation: Sinasabi sa unang pangungusap na ipinagdiriwang ito "tuwing Agosto."

questions.stem:

Ipagdiwang ang pagtatapos ng taon ng pasukan
Palalimin ang pagmamahal ng kabataan sa mga wika ng bansa

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
Each of the applicants ___ required to submit a birth certificate.
questions.explanation: "Each" is singular, so it takes the singular verb "is", even when followed by a plural phrase like "of the applicants".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The list of requirements ___ posted on the bulletin board.
questions.explanation: The subject is "list" (singular), not "requirements". A singular subject takes the singular verb "is".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
Neither the manager nor the clerks ___ aware of the new memo.
questions.explanation: With "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Clerks" is plural, so the verb is "were".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The director, along with her two assistants, ___ attending the seminar.
questions.explanation: Phrases like "along with" do not change the number of the subject. "The director" is singular, so the verb is "is".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The documents were given to Maria and ___.
questions.explanation: After the preposition "to", use the object pronoun "me". Test it by dropping "Maria and": "given to me".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
Between you and ___, the report is not yet finished.
questions.explanation: "Between" is a preposition, so it takes object pronouns: "between you and me".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
She is the employee ___ received the service award.
questions.explanation: "Who" is the subject of the verb "received". Use "whom" only for objects, and "which" for things, not people.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
To ___ should the complaint be addressed?
questions.explanation: After the preposition "to", the object form "whom" is required.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The office will be closed ___ Monday because of the holiday.
questions.explanation: Use "on" with specific days and dates (on Monday, on June 12), "in" with months and years, and "at" with clock times.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The seminar starts ___ 8:00 a.m.
questions.explanation: Use "at" for specific clock times.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
By the time the inspector arrived, the workers ___ the site.
questions.explanation: The past perfect "had left" shows an action completed before another past action (the inspector's arrival).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
If I ___ the head of the agency, I would simplify the process.
questions.explanation: Hypothetical or contrary-to-fact conditions use the subjunctive "were" for all subjects: "If I were...".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The new procedure will ___ the waiting time of clients.
questions.explanation: "Affect" is usually the verb meaning to influence; "effect" is usually the noun meaning a result.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The agency posted ___ new Citizen's Charter at the entrance.
questions.explanation: "Its" is the possessive form, which is needed here. "It's" means "it is" or "it has", and "its'" is never correct.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The applicants left ___ folders at the reception desk.
questions.explanation: "Their" is the possessive form. "There" refers to a place, and "they're" means "they are".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
There were ___ complaints this month than last month.
questions.explanation: Use "fewer" with countable nouns (complaints) and "less" with uncountable nouns (less time, less water).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
Of the two proposals, the second one is ___ than the first.
questions.explanation: "Than" calls for the comparative form of "good," which is "better." "More better" is a double comparative.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The number of online applicants ___ increased this year.
questions.explanation: "The number of..." is singular and takes "has". By contrast, "a number of applicants" means several applicants and takes a plural verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: A third-person singular subject takes "doesn't" followed by the base form of the verb: "She doesn't know".

questions.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: The clerk, who was new, made several errors.
The clerk who was new, made several errors.
The clerk, who was new made several errors.
The clerk who, was new, made several errors.
questions.explanation: A non-essential clause is set off by a pair of commas, one before and one after: "The clerk, who was new, made several errors."

questions.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: Walking to the office, I saw a long line of applicants.
Walking to the office, a long line of applicants was seen.
Walking to the office, the applicants' line was long.
A long line of applicants, walking to the office, I saw.
questions.explanation: An introductory participle phrase must describe the subject that follows it. Only "I" can be the one walking; the other options are dangling modifiers.

questions.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: Neither of the two offices is open on Sunday.
Neither of the two offices are open on Sunday.
Neither of the two office is open on Sunday.
Neither of the two offices were open on Sunday.
questions.explanation: "Neither" used as a pronoun is singular and takes "is".

questions.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: The supervisor asked us to complete the forms quickly and accurately.
The supervisor asked us to complete the forms quick and accurate.
The supervisor asked us to complete the forms quickly and accurate.
The supervisor asked us to complete the forms quick and accurately.
questions.explanation: Adverbs modify verbs. Both "quickly" and "accurately" describe how to complete, and parallel structure needs both in adverb form.

questions.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: The applicants were asked to bring a pen, a photo, and an ID.
The applicants were asked to bring a pen, a photo, and ID's.
The applicants were asked to bringing a pen, a photo, and an ID.
The applicants was asked to bring a pen, a photo, and an ID.
questions.explanation: Plural subject "applicants" takes "were". "To" is followed by the base verb "bring", and the list items are parallel.

questions.stem:
Identify the error in the sentence.
The new employees (A) has been (B) assigned to (C) the records section (D).
questions.explanation: The plural subject "employees" needs the plural verb "have been", not "has been".

questions.stem:
Identify the error in the sentence.
My colleague and me (A) were sent (B) to the regional office (C) last week (D).
questions.explanation: The subject needs the subject pronoun: "My colleague and I were sent...".

questions.stem:
Identify the error in the sentence.
The report must be submitted (A) by Friday, (B) irregardless of (C) the delay in data gathering (D).
questions.explanation: "Irregardless" is nonstandard. Use "regardless of".

questions.stem:
Identify the error in the sentence.
The supervisor (A) gave the instructions (B) to Ana and I (C) this morning (D).
questions.explanation: After the preposition "to", use the object pronoun: "to Ana and me". Test it by dropping "Ana and": "to me".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The staff were told to ___ their reports before the deadline.
questions.explanation: After "to", use the base form of the verb: "to proofread".

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The chairman insisted that every member ___ present at the hearing.
questions.explanation: Verbs of demand or insistence take the subjunctive base form: "insisted that every member be present".

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. As a result, residents no longer have to travel to the city hall for simple requests.
B. Last year, the municipality opened satellite offices in three distant barangays.
C. Each office can issue barangay clearances, community tax certificates, and business permit forms.
D. The mayor now plans to open two more offices next year.
questions.explanation: B introduces the satellite offices, C describes what each office does, A gives the result, and D looks ahead to next year.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. First, the applicant fills out the application form and attaches the required documents.
B. Applying for a passport involves a few simple steps.
C. Finally, the applicant returns on the release date to claim the passport.
D. Next, the applicant appears at the scheduled appointment for photo and biometrics capture.
questions.explanation: B is the topic sentence; the signal words First (A), Next (D) and Finally (C) give the order of the steps.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. These trees absorb carbon dioxide and release the oxygen we breathe.
B. Forests are often called the lungs of the Earth.
C. When forests are cleared, this natural exchange is lost.
D. That is why reforestation programs are an important part of fighting climate change.
questions.explanation: B introduces forests; A ("These trees") explains why; C ("this natural exchange") refers back to A; D draws the conclusion.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. However, many applicants did not see the notice and missed the deadline.
B. The agency moved its application deadline from June to April this year.
C. To avoid a repeat, the agency will now announce changes at least three months in advance.
D. It posted the new schedule only on its website.
questions.explanation: B states the change, D tells how it was announced, A (However) gives the problem that followed, and C gives the agency's fix.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. She saved part of her salary every payday for three years.
B. Liza had long dreamed of opening a small bakery in her hometown.
C. With those savings and a small loan, she finally rented a space near the public market.
D. Today, her bakery employs five people from the neighborhood.
questions.explanation: B introduces Liza and her dream, A describes her saving, C ("those savings") follows from A, and D (Today) ends the story.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. The heat is trapped by gases such as carbon dioxide and methane.
B. Sunlight passes through the atmosphere and warms the Earth's surface.
C. The surface then gives off part of this energy as heat.
D. This trapping effect is what scientists call the greenhouse effect.
questions.explanation: The process runs in order: sunlight warms the surface (B), the surface gives off heat (C), gases trap that heat (A), and D names the effect.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. For example, a business owner in Quezon City can renew a permit through the city's website.
B. Many local governments have moved their services online.
C. Doing so takes only a few minutes instead of a whole day in line.
D. However, offices still keep a help desk for those without internet access.
questions.explanation: B is the general statement, A gives an example, C ("Doing so") refers to renewing online in A, and D (However) adds a qualification.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. Then, a committee interviews the shortlisted candidates.
B. Hiring in government follows a merit-based process.
C. The appointing authority makes the final selection from the top-ranked candidates.
D. First, the human resource office screens applications against the qualification standards.
questions.explanation: B introduces the process; First (D), Then (A), and the final selection (C) give the order of the steps.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. Mix the ingredients well and pour the batter into a greased pan.
B. Bake for thirty minutes, then let the cake cool before slicing.
C. Preheat the oven before you start preparing the batter.
D. Making a simple cake is easier than many people think.
questions.explanation: D introduces the topic, then the steps follow in cooking order: preheat (C), mix and pour (A), bake and cool (B).

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. Instead, it was caused by a faulty electrical connection in the storage room.
B. Investigators first suspected that the fire started in the kitchen.
C. The building owner has since replaced all the old wiring.
D. Their report, however, showed that the kitchen was undamaged.
questions.explanation: B gives the first suspicion, D (however) rules it out, A (Instead) gives the real cause, and C tells what was done afterward.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. Because of this, the Philippines experiences many earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
B. The Philippines lies along the Pacific Ring of Fire.
C. This is a belt of active faults and volcanoes surrounding the Pacific Ocean.
D. Residents are therefore encouraged to join regular earthquake drills.
questions.explanation: B names the Ring of Fire, C ("This is") defines it, A (Because of this) gives the effect, and D (therefore) gives the advice that follows.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. Despite her success, she continued to live simply.
B. Rosa grew up in a fishing village and walked two kilometers to school every day.
C. She later earned a scholarship and graduated with honors in accountancy.
D. She now spends her weekends tutoring children from her old village.
questions.explanation: The story runs in time order: childhood (B), later success (C), how she lived despite it (A), and what she does now (D).

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. The law requires every barangay or cluster of barangays to set up a materials recovery facility.
B. Republic Act No. 9003 was passed to address the country's growing waste problem.
C. In such a facility, collected waste is sorted, recycled, or composted.
D. Only residual waste that cannot be processed is brought to disposal sites.
questions.explanation: B introduces the law, A ("The law") gives its requirement, C ("such a facility") describes it, and D tells what happens to what is left.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. When she checked the records, she found that the payment had been posted to the wrong account.
B. A client complained that his payment did not appear in his account.
C. She corrected the entry and called the client to apologize.
D. The clerk on duty promised to look into the problem.
questions.explanation: B states the complaint, D introduces the clerk, A ("she") describes what the clerk found, and C tells how she fixed it.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. Without enough sleep, the body cannot repair itself properly.
B. Sleep is as important to health as diet and exercise.
C. Over time, this can weaken the immune system and affect concentration.
D. Experts therefore recommend seven to nine hours of sleep each night for adults.
questions.explanation: B is the main idea, A explains why, C ("this") builds on A, and D (therefore) gives the recommendation.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. The first one was held in 2019 and drew only twenty participants.
B. The city holds an annual coastal cleanup every September.
C. Last year, more than five hundred volunteers joined.
D. Its growth shows how much residents now care about their shoreline.
questions.explanation: B introduces the cleanup, A ("The first one") goes back to its start, C shows its recent size, and D comments on the growth.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. Unfortunately, the typhoon damaged the bridge two weeks before the opening.
B. The new bridge was supposed to open in July.
C. Repairs pushed the opening back to October.
D. Commuters who had expected a shorter trip to work will have to wait a few more months.
questions.explanation: B gives the plan, A (Unfortunately) the setback, C the new date, and D the effect on commuters.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. Second, it must be signed by the person making it.
B. A valid affidavit must meet several requirements.
C. Lastly, it must be sworn to before a notary public or another authorized officer.
D. First, it must be in writing.
questions.explanation: B introduces the requirements; First (D), Second (A), and Lastly (C) give their order.

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. Within minutes, smoke filled the hallway.
B. The fire alarm rang at exactly 2:00 p.m.
C. Thanks to the drill they had done the week before, all employees left the building safely.
D. Firefighters arrived soon after and put out the fire in the storage room.
questions.explanation: The events run in time order: the alarm (B), smoke within minutes (A), the safe evacuation (C), and firefighters arriving after (D).

questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical paragraph.
A. They also learn to manage their time between school and work.
B. Many senior high school students take part-time jobs during summer.
C. These jobs teach them responsibility and the value of money.
D. Because of these benefits, schools are encouraged to help students find safe summer work.
questions.explanation: B introduces the topic, C ("These jobs") gives a first benefit, A ("also") adds a second, and D ("these benefits") concludes.

questions.stem:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

The town of San Rafael once struggled with garbage piling up along its creek. Instead of buying more trucks, the municipal government trained household volunteers to separate biodegradable waste from recyclables. Within a year, the volume of garbage sent to the dumpsite fell by almost half, and the money saved was used to build a small composting facility.

What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Composting facilities are expensive to build.
The creek in San Rafael is now completely clean.
Training households to segregate waste reduced garbage and saved money.
San Rafael bought more garbage trucks to clean its creek.
questions.explanation: The passage describes how household segregation, rather than more trucks, cut garbage nearly in half and freed funds for composting. The passage never says the creek is completely clean.

questions.stem:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

Instead of buying more trucks, the municipal government trained household volunteers to separate biodegradable waste from recyclables. Within a year, the volume of garbage sent to the dumpsite fell by almost half, and the money saved was used to build a small composting facility.

According to the passage, how was the money saved used?
choices: To build a small composting facility
questions.explanation: The last sentence states that the money saved was used to build a small composting facility.

questions.stem:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

The town of San Rafael once struggled with garbage piling up along its creek. Instead of buying more trucks, the municipal government trained household volunteers to separate biodegradable waste from recyclables. Within a year, the volume of garbage sent to the dumpsite fell by almost half, and the money saved was used to build a small composting facility.

Which can be inferred from the passage?
choices: The town's earlier approach was less effective than involving households.
Other towns in the province have already copied San Rafael's program.
The dumpsite will be closed once the composting facility is finished.
The household volunteers were paid from the money that was saved.
questions.explanation: The contrast between the old problem and the result after involving households implies the earlier approach worked less well. The other choices add facts the passage never gives.

questions.stem:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

Many government offices now post a Citizen's Charter at their entrance. The charter lists each service the office provides, the documents required, the steps to follow, the fees, and the maximum time each step should take. By making these standards public, the charter allows clients to know what to expect and gives them a basis for complaining when service falls short.

According to the passage, which of the following is NOT listed in a Citizen's Charter?
choices: The maximum time for each step
The names of employees who were disciplined
questions.explanation: The passage lists services, required documents, steps, fees, and maximum processing times. It says nothing about disciplined employees.

questions.stem:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

Many government offices now post a Citizen's Charter at their entrance. The charter lists each service the office provides, the documents required, the steps to follow, the fees, and the maximum time each step should take. By making these standards public, the charter allows clients to know what to expect and gives them a basis for complaining when service falls short.

What is the purpose of making service standards public, according to the passage?
choices: So clients know what to expect and can complain when service falls short
So offices can charge higher fees
So the office does not need to answer questions
So employees can work fewer hours
questions.explanation: The final sentence gives both purposes: clients know what to expect and have a basis for complaints.

questions.stem:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

As used in the passage, the phrase "falls short" most nearly means:
choices: costs less than the posted fee
questions.explanation: Service that "falls short" fails to reach the posted standards, which is why it gives clients a basis for complaint.

questions.stem:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

Mangrove forests protect coastal communities in ways that are easy to overlook. Their tangled roots slow down waves and reduce the force of storm surges, while also trapping soil that would otherwise wash into the sea. The roots also shelter young fish and crabs, so fishermen who live near healthy mangroves often enjoy better catches. Despite this, many mangrove areas have been cleared for fishponds and housing.

Which title best fits the passage?
choices: The Dangers of Fishing at Sea
questions.explanation: The passage explains several hidden benefits of mangroves (storm protection, soil retention, fish nurseries) and notes they are still being cleared.

choices: Storm surges bring in more fish.
The roots shelter young fish and crabs.
questions.explanation: The passage states that the roots shelter young fish and crabs, which leads to better catches.

questions.stem:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

When the provincial hospital introduced an online appointment system, older patients at first complained that they did not know how to use it. The hospital responded by keeping two walk-in windows open and assigning volunteers to help patients book on their phones. After six months, waiting times had dropped and complaints had nearly disappeared.

How did the hospital respond to the older patients' complaints?
choices: It required all patients to book online.
It cancelled the online appointment system.
It kept walk-in windows open and assigned volunteers to help with booking.
questions.explanation: The second sentence describes the response: two walk-in windows stayed open and volunteers helped patients book.

questions.stem:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

When the provincial hospital introduced an online appointment system, older patients at first complained that they did not know how to use it. The hospital responded by keeping two walk-in windows open and assigning volunteers to help patients book on their phones. After six months, waiting times had dropped and complaints had nearly disappeared.

Which lesson is best supported by the passage?
choices: New systems work better when users who struggle with them are given support.
Walk-in windows are always faster than online booking.
Online systems should never be used in hospitals.
Older patients refuse to learn new technology.
questions.explanation: The passage shows that the system succeeded once struggling users got help and an alternative. The other choices overgeneralize or contradict the passage.

questions.stem:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

Long lines and repeated trips to government offices were once a common complaint among Filipinos. To address this, offices have been required to set clear processing times for each service and to publish them. Simple transactions are expected to be completed within three working days, while complex ones are given up to seven. Offices that fail to meet these standards without valid reason may face administrative sanctions. The goal is not only speed but also predictability: citizens should know in advance how long a transaction will take and what documents they will need.

What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Long lines are caused by a lack of government employees.
Government offices are being required to make their services faster and more predictable.
All government transactions now take exactly three days.
questions.explanation: The passage is about required processing times that make services both faster and predictable. It never blames a lack of employees.

questions.stem:
Read the passage, then answer the question.

Cities are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them, a pattern known as the urban heat island effect. Concrete and asphalt absorb sunlight during the day and release the stored heat slowly at night, so cities stay warm even after sunset. Trees and green spaces counter this effect by providing shade and cooling the air as water evaporates from their leaves. For this reason, some city planners now require new developments to set aside space for parks and tree-lined streets.

According to the passage, why do cities stay warm after sunset?
choices: Concrete and asphalt release heat they absorbed during the day.
Cities receive more sunlight than the countryside.
Water evaporates more slowly in cities.
Trees release stored heat at night.

Cities are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them, a pattern known as the urban heat island effect. Concrete and asphalt absorb sunlight during the day and release the stored heat slowly at night, so cities stay warm even after sunset. Trees and green spaces counter this effect by providing shade and cooling the air as water evaporates from their leaves. For this reason, some city planners now require new developments to set aside space for parks and tree-lined streets.

Why do some city planners require new developments to set aside space for parks?

questions.explanation: Parks and trees "counter this effect," which is why planners require them ("For this reason").

The traditional image of bayanihan shows neighbors carrying a whole house on bamboo poles to a new location. Few families move houses this way today, but the spirit behind the practice survives. Some sociologists argue that this habit of mutual help is one reason Filipino communities recover from disasters as quickly as they do.
